newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's bond yields fall on improving liquidity.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's bond yields fall on improving liquidity.

text.p: Yields on three-year benchmark corporate bonds closed lower on Thursday on market talks that the central bank would remain flexible on money supply for the time being, traders said.
They said fears of liquidity squeeze have now faded and institutional investors bought actively.
However, the yields are likely to rebound on Friday after hitting a low of 12.70 percent, they said.
* Overnight average call rates at 13.72 vs 13.84
Traders said the central bank was widely expected to absorb the excess liquidity on Friday through repurchase agreements.
"The corporate yields are expected to move around the 12.70 percent level tomorrow," a local dealer said.
Three-month CD yields and overnight call rates also declined on better liquidity conditions.
